Every direction claim this build made and got wrong, mapped to the executed case
that now discharges it.

**What a direction claim is.** An inference of the form *because I observed A, B
holds*. It is called a direction claim because the inference runs one way:
observing A may establish B while the absence of A establishes nothing. A check
written without noticing which way its own inference runs will report the strong
direction and mean the weak one.

**What the exhibits share.** An observation was scored as positive evidence for a proposition it could not support, and the check that should have caught the gap passed instead. In every case the passing result was real — the check did run and did return true — and the proposition it was read as establishing was false. The failure is never in the observation; it is in the direction the inference was allowed to run.

## EX-1 — The demo plugin that every spelling of "off" installed

*Register: D-009, OF-003 · Obligations: B10*

**The claim.** Because OPENC3_DEMO in the deployment environment equals the string generated from defs/ground.yaml's `demo_targets: false` — the literal "0" — the demo plugin is not installed, and therefore the targets present in HUGINN's COSMOS instance are exactly the targets this repository generated.

**What was actually established.** That the variable held the string "0". Nothing about what the container did with it. openc3-cosmos-init's /openc3/init.sh tests `[ ! -z $OPENC3_DEMO ]` — presence, not value — so "0", "false" and "1" all install the demo, and only an empty value or absence suppresses it.

**Why the check missed it.** The retired G16 property was falsified only BETWEEN TWO VALUES THAT BOTH INSTALL. Its red case flipped 0 to 1 and both spellings load the demo, so the mutation could not distinguish a correct configuration from the defect. A red case that moves along an axis the subject does not respond to certifies whatever it is pointed at.

The loaded-vs-repository check ruled at D-010 is what closes that gap, and it is executed by tools/pass_setup.py as PROC-001's pre-pass step rather than by the gate — so the gate's green does not by itself establish the deployed instance.

## EX-2 — The staleness monitor that annunciated without ever reading

*Register: OF-002, D-012 · Obligations: B6*

**The claim.** Because the ground-side monitor annunciated GREEN then YELLOW at 10 s then RED at 30 s, at exactly the dictionary's spacing, the monitor observed CDH_FRAME_CNT stop advancing.

**What was actually established.** That thirty seconds of wall-clock had passed since the monitor's process started. The generated monitor computed staleness from process start rather than from its first successful read, and swallowed every read failure, so a monitor that had never once read the counter produced a transcript indistinguishable from one watching a real halt.

**Why the check missed it.** Nothing asked the monitor to prove it had ever looked. The demonstration scored the annunciation sequence, which a dead monitor emits just as readily as a live one, and the sequence was the whole of the evidence.

| `test_staleness_monitor.TestTheDeadMonitorCannotProduceTheTranscript.test_the_dead_monitor_ran_long_enough_for_red_to_have_fired` | red | yes | PASS |

**Residual.** The GREEN-ENTRY control — that the monitor was restarted and observed ENTERING GREEN inside the run's own window — is archived in the B6 manifest as artifacts/green-entry.txt but is not re-derived from the archive by b6_verdict. The control that makes every later level trustworthy is therefore the one clause of the B6 verdict a reader must still take on the manifest's word.

## EX-3 — The monitor that latched when its reads stopped working

*Register: OF-006, D-012 · Obligations: B6*

**The claim.** Because the monitor annunciated a staleness LEVEL and has said nothing since, the spacecraft's frame counter is in the state last annunciated, observed by a working read path.

**What was actually established.** That the monitor emitted a level at some past instant. Two inferences were bundled and both run one way: a level implies a read only if reads cannot fail silently, and silence implies no change only if the monitor logs on every poll rather than on transition. Neither held. A read path that broke after one success left the last level latched and the log quiet.

**Why the check missed it.** Transition-only logging makes silence ambiguous by construction, and the vocabulary had no way to say "I cannot see". D-012 supplied READ_FAULT (the path worked and stopped) and NO_READ (it never worked), which is what makes the two distinguishable in a transcript at all.

**Executed cases.**

| Case | Declared | Ran | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_staleness_monitor.TestARealHaltIsStillCaught.test_a_read_failure_AFTER_a_successful_read_is_a_READ_FAULT_not_staleness` | red | yes | PASS |
| `test_staleness_monitor.TestARealHaltIsStillCaught.test_the_read_fault_annunciation_names_the_ground_segment` | red | yes | PASS |
| `test_staleness_monitor.TestARealHaltIsStillCaught.test_staleness_across_a_read_outage_is_not_erased_by_recovery` | red | yes | PASS |
| `test_b6_verdict.TestAReadFaultBreaksTheObservation.test_a_read_fault_in_the_transcript_fails` | red | yes | PASS |

**Residual.** b6_verdict refuses a transcript containing READ_FAULT but does not refuse one containing NO_READ. A monitor that never read at all is the more serious of the two conditions and is the one the verdict does not currently reject.

## EX-4 — Two negative controls that a SyntaxError satisfied

*Register: OF-008, OF-005 · Obligations: B14*

**The claim.** Because the ground system's own reader, invoked against a path that does not exist, emitted no PACKETS line, it returned no packets; therefore the playback was bound to the named native log file rather than to the runtime databases.

**What was actually established.** That no PACKETS line appeared. Both controls built their command by joining simple statements with semicolons and then appending a compound statement, which is a SyntaxError — so neither control's script ever compiled and neither ever ran. Both were scored on an ABSENCE (`file_bound = control_count == 0`), and an absence is exactly what a program that never started produces.

**Why the check missed it.** A control scored on an absence cannot distinguish "ran and observed nothing" from "never ran". The control could not have failed, which is the same as saying it was not a control.

**Executed cases.**

| `test_b14_verdict.TestAControlThatNeverRan.test_a_control_that_failed_for_a_different_reason` | red | yes | PASS |

**Residual.** Covered under D-013 item 1, closing OF-012. `b14_verdict` re-derives B14 from the archived bytes alone, as b6_verdict and b11_verdict do for their obligations, and every control it scores must show the reader ACTUALLY RAN — a `REFUSED <ExceptionType>` line only an executed reader produces. The zero-count line the original controls were scored on is still required and is never sufficient by itself, because an absence is not an observation. The two red cases that matter remove only the evidence of execution and assert the absence clause still holds, so they fail against the verdict B14 shipped with and pass against this one. One residual remains: the SyntaxError transcript that diagnosed OF-008 exists only as prose in this register. The artifact was overwritten before the evidence harness was capturing, so the defect itself is recorded rather than archived.

## EX-5 — Every evidence digest had stopped verifying

*Register: OF-009, D-008 · Obligations: B6, B7, B10, B11, B14*

**The claim.** Because every manifest carries a sha256 per artifact, what the gate reads can be shown to be what the demonstration produced.

**What was actually established.** That a digest had been written down beside a filename. Nothing recomputed it. Evidence captured on Windows held CRLF, and .gitattributes' `* text=auto eol=lf` meant git stored a translated copy of every text artifact while the manifest recorded the digest of the untranslated bytes. On a fresh clone not one digest would have verified.

**Why the check missed it.** There was no check. The digests were written and never read back, so the binding the ruling relied on existed only as an intention. This is the one exhibit whose defect would have been invisible to a reader rather than merely misleading: the artifacts were present, readable, and no longer what they claimed to be.

**Executed cases.**

| Case | Declared | Ran | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_verify_evidence.TestTamperingIsCaught.test_a_line_ending_translation_fails` | red | yes | PASS |
| `test_verify_evidence.TestTamperingIsCaught.test_an_edited_artifact_fails` | red | yes | PASS |
| `test_verify_evidence.TestTamperingIsCaught.test_a_missing_artifact_fails` | red | yes | PASS |
| `test_verify_evidence.TestVacuousPassesAreRefused.test_an_empty_evidence_root_fails` | red | yes | PASS |
| `test_verify_evidence.TestVacuousPassesAreRefused.test_a_manifest_listing_no_artifacts_fails` | red | yes | PASS |
| `test_verify_evidence.TestIntactEvidenceVerifies.test_an_untouched_attempt_passes` | green | yes | PASS |

**Residual.** tools/verify_evidence.py now recomputes every digest on every gate run, and the line-ending case is the one that matters — same text, different bytes — because a check comparing content rather than bytes would pass it and miss precisely what happened.

## EX-6 — A red case caught by a crash rather than by its check

*Register: OF-011 · Obligations: B4*

**The claim.** Because G11.m1 turns G11 red when an FMEA severity rating is moved outside the Sec. 3 definitions, G11 detects out-of-range ratings.

**What was actually established.** That G11 does not survive the input. G11's own detection at the top of the function had already found the violation and appended it to `problems`, but execution continued into the R2 partition, whose risk_of() lookup raised KeyError on the undefined rating before the finding could be returned. The self-test scored the crash as CAUGHT.

**Why the check missed it.** The self-test's red criterion was "the check did not return true", and a check that raises does not return true. Crash and detection are indistinguishable under that criterion — OF-008's shape, one level down, inside the machinery that certifies every other check.

**Executed cases.**

| Case | Declared | Ran | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| `defs_generation:G11.m1` | red | yes | PASS |
| `defs_generation:G11.m3` | red | yes | PASS |

**Residual.** Found while building this phase's observation layer, which records passed_by_exception per mutation case for exactly this reason. G11 now returns its finding before deriving risk it cannot derive. One instance existed in the build; the run record now reports the count, so a second cannot arrive quietly.

## EX-7 — A validator that refused the record its own procedure ordered

*Register: OF-010 · Obligations: B13*

**The claim.** Because the B13 completion-record suite is green across 63 two-polarity cases built from the procedure definition itself, the completion-record contract is the contract the procedures require.

**What was actually established.** That the contract is self-consistent about STEPS. The fixtures were generated from the procedures' step list, and both defects lived in the BRANCHES — in the `then:` text that tells an operator what to do next. PROC-001-S03's no-go branch orders S02 re-run and S12's ARG_RANGE branch orders a re-send, while the validator allowed each step exactly one entry; PROC-001-S05 and S07 hand off to PROC-003 and PROC-002 with nowhere in the report to record the contingency work.

**Why the check missed it.** A generated fixture inherits the blind spot of the field it generates from. Every case was derived from `steps`, so no case could exercise an obligation stated in `branches`.

**Executed cases.**

| Case | Declared | Ran | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_pass_report.TestInPassReExecution.test_green_a_described_re_run_is_accepted` | green | yes | PASS |
| `test_pass_report.TestInPassReExecution.test_red_a_second_entry_is_still_refused` | red | yes | PASS |
| `test_pass_report.TestInPassReExecution.test_red_a_counted_attempt_that_is_never_described` | red | yes | PASS |
| `test_pass_report.TestAPassThatInvokesAContingencyProcedure.test_red_the_invoking_step_took_a_different_branch` | red | yes | PASS |
| `test_pass_report.TestAPassThatInvokesAContingencyProcedure.test_green_a_contingency_procedure_run_from_its_branch` | green | yes | PASS |

**Why this one is admitted, and how it differs.** THIS EXHIBIT IS A DIFFERENT SPECIES AND IS ADMITTED SAYING SO. The other six are checks that PASSED on a false proposition — they were silent, and silence is why they survived. OF-010's validator FAILED, loudly, on a true record; a tool that refuses something true announces itself the first time an operator meets it. On that difference alone it would be a correctness defect and not an evidence-chain exhibit. It is admitted because of what it would have produced downstream. An operator who followed PROC-001-S03, went no-go, reloaded and re-ran had exactly one conforming record available: the one that reports the successful attempt and omits the failed one. The contract would have manufactured a record of a pass that went right the first time, from an operator doing everything correctly — which is the same false evidence the other six exhibits produce, arriving by the opposite route. And the framing claim above ("63 green cases, therefore the contract is right") is a direction claim that failed for a locatable reason. Recorded here as EX-7 with this note rather than either folded in silently or left out. THE STRONGEST OBJECTION TO ADMITTING IT, STATED SO THE DIRECTOR CAN RULE AGAINST ME. The false record OF-010 would have produced has NO INSTANCE and never had one. The campaign has not run; the only pass report in the repository is a worked example. No operator was refused, no failed attempt was dropped, no pass ever read as a first-time GO. The downstream consequence argued above is REASONED, not MEASURED — and every other exhibit here was measured: D-009's polarity table was taken from the container at five settings, the monitor was observed annunciating while dead, the B14 controls were run and found never to have compiled, the digests were recomputed and did not match. On the evidence standard the other six meet, EX-7 is the only entry resting on an argument rather than an observation. It is admitted because the direction claim about the CHECKER did occur and is measurable — the 63 cases were green and the contract was incomplete — but a reader should know the two halves are not equally grounded.
